rics.meaning: Employment in Agriculture, Forestry, Hunting & Fishery — workers in primary sectors. ~28% of total employment but only ~13% of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Productivity-gap measure: employment share much higher than GDP share signals low-productivity informal-rural employment. Structural decline from ~40% (2010) to ~28% (2024) reflects urbanization.

rics.meaning: Employment, Annual Total — BPS annual labor-force employment level. Aggregate of formal + informal sector employed.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia total employment ~135-140M. Annual frequency cleaner for trend. Watch for capacity-utilization signals: sustained employment gains alongside flat output point to labor-productivity headwinds.

rics.meaning: Employment in Community, Social & Personal Services — workers in education, healthcare, government services, household services.
rics.how_to_use: Stable, counter-cyclical category. Government employment dominates (civil servants, teachers, healthcare workers). Public-sector hiring decisions drive trend.

rics.meaning: Employment in Construction — workers employed in residential, commercial, infrastructure construction. ~7% of total employment.
rics.how_to_use: Highly cyclical with infrastructure spending and BI rates. Surged during 2014-2024 infrastructure push; decelerated since. Watch alongside cement consumption.

rics.meaning: Employment in Electricity, Gas & Water — utility-sector workers. Small share (<1%) but high productivity.
rics.how_to_use: Stable, low-cyclicality. Tracks state-owned utility (PLN) employment patterns plus IPP (independent power producer) staffing.

rics.description: Employment, Financing, insurance, real estate, business service
rics.meaning: Employment in Financing, Insurance, Real Estate, Business Services — white-collar professional employment.
rics.how_to_use: Indicator of services-economy maturation. Tracks bank, insurance, asset-management, professional-services hiring. Concentrated in Jakarta/major cities.

rics.meaning: Employment in Manufacturing — workers employed in the manufacturing sector. ~14% of total employment but ~20% of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Track for manufacturing-cycle signal. Sustained declines flag deindustrialization concerns. Pair with manufacturing GVA (aIDVADGM/C) for productivity calculations.

rics.meaning: Employment in Mining and Quarrying — workers in extractive industries. Small employment share (~1.5%) but high productivity.
rics.how_to_use: Cyclical with commodity prices. Track for major mine closures/openings (Freeport's Grasberg expansion, Newmont/Amman's Batu Hijau). High average wages drive disproportionate income contribution.

rics.meaning: Employment, Quarterly Total — higher-frequency BPS employment release. Captures total employed across sectors.
rics.how_to_use: Use for cyclical tracking between annual Sakernas releases. Quarterly volatility from agricultural seasonality (planting/harvest cycles) is high.

rics.meaning: Employment in Transportation, Storage & Communications — workers in logistics, transport, telecom, ICT services.
rics.how_to_use: Growing share post-2015 with digital economy expansion (Gojek, Grab drivers). E-commerce + ride-hailing have created new employment categories captured here.

rics.description: Employment, Wholesale & retail trade, restaurants, hotels
rics.meaning: Employment in Wholesale & Retail Trade, Restaurants, Hotels — distributive trades + tourism employment. ~22% of total.
rics.how_to_use: Second-largest employment sector after agriculture. Cyclical with consumer spending and tourism flows. Pair with retail sales (aIDRSLSAR) for the distributive-trades cycle.

rics.meaning: Labour Force, Unemployment — total unemployed persons in the labor force. Number of people without work but actively seeking.
rics.how_to_use: Combine with employment count to compute unemployment rate. Indonesia ~7-8M unemployed (2024) out of ~143M labor force.

rics.description: Employment, Employment, Payroll jobs, Standardized (based on source annual data)
rics.meaning: Employment, Payroll Jobs (Standardized) — formal-sector employment level. From BPS Sakernas (Labor Force Survey).
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia formal-sector employment ~50-55M people; informal sector ~80M. Formal-share growth signals labor-market modernization. Track YoY pace for cyclical signal.
